author: DRazwx
quote: When considering the success of the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and its reputation as one of the greatest video games ever made, I had extremely high expectations for its remake. Considering the amount of time that has passed since the original release in 1998, I expected Nintendo to make significant improvements to the gameplay while maintaining the aspects that made the original so successful. However, after looking at what Nintendo has actually changed, I found that many of these changes not only fail to improve the game, but actually take away from what made the original **** of the biggest issues I have with the remake is the gameplay itself. While Nintendo has made improvements to the controls and movement, I feel like these changes are relatively insignificant when considering the problems that still exist. The combat is extremely basic compared to modern games, and many of the enemies provide almost no challenge whatsoever. This is especially disappointing considering Nintendo had the opportunity to expand on the original combat system and make it more engaging. Instead, they actually made certain aspects of the game easier, which I think is a completely unnecessary decision. Because of this, many of the encounters that should feel rewarding end up being extremely underwhelming.Another thing that particularly stood out to me was the amount of unnecessary dialogue and guidance throughout the game. Something that made the original Ocarina of Time so enjoyable was the fact that players were often required to explore and figure things out themselves. However, the remake seems to constantly provide information that the player could have easily discovered without assistance. I think this significantly takes away from the sense of accomplishment that comes from completing puzzles and discovering new areas. While I understand that Nintendo is attempting to make the game more accessible to newer players, I don’t think this justifies removing much of the challenge that made the original so memorable.I also think the changes to the presentation are somewhat disappointing. Although the graphics are obviously significantly better than those of the original, I don’t necessarily think better graphics automatically make a game better. The original had a very distinctive atmosphere that helped establish its identity, and some of the changes to the visuals and voice acting seem to take away from this. This is especially frustrating because I think Nintendo could have maintained much more of the original atmosphere while still making improvements to the graphics. Instead, certain parts of the game feel like they were changed simply for the purpose of making them more modern rather than actually improving the experience.When analyzing the broader impact of these changes, I think the biggest issue is that Nintendo seems to have misunderstood what made Ocarina of Time such an influential game in the first place. While the original was revolutionary for its time, many of its mechanics are now relatively outdated. Because of this, I think a remake should have focused on meaningfully improving these mechanics rather than simply making the game look better and removing some of the difficulty. I also find it disappointing that Nintendo did not include Master Quest, which would have at least provided experienced players with an additional challenge.Overall, I think the Ocarina of Time remake is an extremely disappointing release, especially considering the expectations surrounding it. While the game certainly has some positive aspects, such as its improved graphics and controls, I don’t think these improvements are nearly significant enough to justify many of the other changes. It’s especially disappointing because Nintendo had the opportunity to take one of the most influential games ever made and improve upon it in ways that weren’t possible in 1998. Instead, I feel like we received a visually impressive version of a nearly 30-year-old game that somehow manages to make certain aspects of the original worse. I would give the remake a 3/10, and I genuinely think the original is a more enjoyable experience despite its age.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: DRazwx
quote: When looking at the expectations surrounding GTA 6, it’s difficult to imagine how Rockstar could have possibly made a game that lived up to the amount of anticipation it received. Considering the success of GTA 5 and the amount of time that has passed since its release, I had extremely high expectations for nearly every aspect of the game. Despite this, I genuinely think Rockstar managed to create something that not only meets these expectations, but exceeds them to an extent that I really didn’t think was **** first thing that stood out to me was the amount of detail throughout the world. When exploring Vice City, there is an almost overwhelming amount of things happening around you, whether it’s the people walking around, the traffic, or just the general environment itself. This makes the world feel significantly more realistic than what we’ve seen in previous GTA games. I think this is especially important because a major part of GTA has always been the freedom to explore and do things outside of the main storyline. Because of this, the amount of attention Rockstar put into the world itself makes even the most basic activities entertaining. There were times where I would spend hours simply exploring the map without progressing through the story at all, which I think shows just how much there is to experience.Another thing I found particularly impressive was the overall quality of the missions and characters. Something that I think many open world games struggle with is maintaining the player’s interest throughout the entire storyline. However, GTA 6 manages to avoid this almost entirely. The missions are consistently entertaining, and the characters actually make you interested in what happens next. This is especially impressive when considering just how much content there is throughout the game. I also think the improvements to the gameplay make a massive difference, as nearly everything feels more enjoyable compared to previous Rockstar titles.When considering the broader impact of GTA 6, I think it’s reasonable to say that it has established an entirely new standard for open world games. While there are obviously other games that have managed to create extremely detailed worlds, I really don’t think anything comes close to what Rockstar has accomplished here. It’s not necessarily one specific feature that makes the game so impressive, but rather the combination of so many different aspects that are all done extremely well.Overall, I genuinely struggle to think of anything significant that I dislike about GTA 6. I went into the game expecting it to be one of the best games I’ve ever played, and somehow it still managed to surprise me. I think it is easily the best game Rockstar has ever created and I honestly wouldn’t disagree with anyone who considers it the greatest video game of all time. I would give it a 10/10 without any hesitation, and I think it’s going to be extremely difficult for any other developer to create something that can compete with it.
